missed_mechanisms.name: sack_wire = 65 B constant does not match the shipped ACK wire size (59 B)
missed_mechanisms.evidence: specs/adaptive-transport-engine-spec.md:985 defines `sack_wire` = 28(UDP/IPv4) + 22(handle4+seq2+tag16) + ACK_FRAME_V2 body(15+4·range) = 65 B at 0 ranges. The product emits `ack.encode()` directly into `seam.seal(...)` (runtime.rs:2172, :2001) and IdentitySeam adds ONLY a 16 B tag with no handle and no seq: crates/client-core/src/seam.rs:118-127 `frame.resize(frame.len() + IDENTITY_TAG, 0)`, seam.rs:114 `pub const IDENTITY_TAG: usize = 16;`. ACK V2 body is exactly 15 + 4n (ack.rs:202 doc, :208-228 encode). So the shipped return datagram is 15+16 = 31 B UDP payload = 59 B on IPv4/UDP, i.e. 6 B (9.2%) below the constant that derives ACK_CADENCE_FLOOR (receiver.rs:93), T_SPACING (receiver.rs:115), the sender EAI return term (sender.rs:1395/3271), the w_epoch return-prior (sender.rs:2910) and the PreConverge rtt_floor (sender.rs:1455/5698). Every one of those five [CAL] constants is therefore derived from a header the product does not emit.
missed_mechanisms.suggested_classification: Not a classification — a calibration-provenance defect that should be recorded against the cadence-floor / EAI records (and it sharpens the open question about the post-S2 layout, since noise-wire's EXTENDED outer would re-derive it a third way).

Neither the cadence floor nor the episode quota can suppress it (the quota is only decremented at :341, never checked as a precondition on this path). corrected_classifications.mechanism: ACK-only return budget fraction Y (RETURN_BUDGET_FRACTION=0.25) / per-profile ACK budget (INV-ACK-1 'ACK-only budgeted')
corrected_classifications.reason: SHIP is not defensible. Y has no independent existence on the product path — it is a compile-time factor inside ACK_CADENCE_FLOOR_NS (receiver.rs:93-94), already fully credited to the cadence-floor record; counting it twice inflates the SHIP list. The normative requirement it is meant to satisfy is disconnected on three counts: (a) no per-profile ACK budget field exists in RuntimeConfig (grep of runtime.rs:85-207 shows quota_r as the only ACK-adjacent knob); (b) receiver.rs:84 scopes Y to 'SACK+echo' but CS-echo (runtime.rs:2311-2323), RECOVERED (:2216/:2305/:2370) and PARAM_ACK (:2352) never enter Receiver's accounting; (c) the only enforcement hook, EgressPolicy, is None in the shipping ServerEndpoint::bind (runtime.rs:311) with a bench-only impl (kama_product.rs:65). INV-ACK-1 (transport-layer-tdd.md §14 L739) is spec-required and structurally unmet → WIRE.

KEEP-EXPERIMENTAL is defined as 'intentionally outside v1, must be default OFF' — that presupposes an artifact whose default state can be checked. There is none: grep -rni piggyback over crates returns only five comment lines inside test harnesses (live_budget_sweep.rs:2, m1_reverse_nis.rs:12,491, micro_sweep_1b.rs:6,423). The record describes a spec sentence (transport-layer-tdd.md §12, non-MUST), not code. It should be struck from the mechanism inventory (or moved to an explicit 'not-implemented, spec-optional' list) so the KEEP-EXPERIMENTAL bucket keeps its meaning: things that exist and must stay off.

corrected_classifications.mechanism: ACK-path diagnostic metrics (ack_loss_rate, ack_compression_score, ack_spacing_rate) — TDD §9 NetworkClassifier
corrected_classifications.reason: Same defect as the piggyback record: nothing exists to keep default-OFF. `grep -rn 'ack_compression|ack_loss_rate|ack_spacing' crates --include=*.rs` returns zero hits across the entire tree including tests. The record is a spec enumeration, not a mechanism. The substantive content — that AC-6 is met structurally by bw.rs:105 `interval_ns = ack_elapsed.max(send_elapsed)` and that the wired reverse-path fuzzy input is ack_confidence_permille (sender.rs:3414) — belongs as a note on the ack_confidence record.

corrected_classifications.mechanism: ACK/SACK frame codec — ACK_FRAME_V2 (0x14) emit, V1 (0x10) decode-compat
corrected_classifications.reason: Classification stands for the V2 emit + decode surface, but the record must be split: the V1 EMIT branch (ack.rs:209-213 `else { FRAME_TYPE_ACK }`) is unreachable product code — `from_received` hardwires v2:true (ack.rs:145) and `grep -rn 'v2: false' crates` returns nothing repo-wide, so no code path in the workspace can construct a V1 frame outside ack.rs:398/:423 test fixtures. That sub-branch plus the client's V1 accept-gate (runtime.rs:1149 `plain[0] != FRAME_TYPE_ACK && ...`) is a DELETE candidate: it widens the accepted-input surface for a codepoint no peer in this system emits, and the tv_ack.rs:47 'V1 compat golden' test pins compatibility with a producer that does not exist.

corrected_classifications.mechanism: Extended SACK V2 measurement ext — emission (seen_count real; arrival_rate = 0xFFFF sentinel per spec zeyl)
corrected_classifications.reason: Classification stands for seen_count (spec §2.2 normative field, really populated at receiver.rs:196). But arrival_rate is not an 'emission mechanism' — it is a hardwired compile-time constant: receiver.rs:477 passes `crate::ack::ARRIVAL_RATE_SENTINEL` unconditionally, and receiver.rs:472-475 documents that the receiver structurally cannot measure it (RxDatagram carries no size). That is 2 B of invariant payload on every SACK (≈6.5% of the 31 B plain frame, ≈3.4% of the 59 B shipped datagram) with neither a producer that can vary it nor a consumer that reads it. The field should be recorded separately as DELETE-or-defer-to-K3, not folded into a SHIP record — otherwise the audit reports as 'shipped' two bytes whose only possible value is a sentinel.

corrected_classifications.mechanism: Extended SACK V2 measurement ext — sender consumer (seen≪sent forward/return-loss split; arrival_rate cold-start bw hint) [K3]
corrected_classifications.reason: KEEP-EXPERIMENTAL again presupposes default-OFF code; there is none (`grep -rn '\.seen_count|\.arrival_rate' crates` yields only ack.rs encode + tests, and AckInfo at sender.rs:944-949 has exactly two fields). More importantly the finding's own spec_requires_v1='experimental' is contradicted by its cited spec text: §2.2 L189-193 states the sender comparison as the PURPOSE of the field pair and §16.1's sack_wire row already charges the 6 B to every ACK. So the workspace unconditionally pays the wire cost of a spec-motivated feature whose consumer is absent — that is the definition of WIRE (spec-required, disconnected), not of an experiment. If the owner rules K3 out of v1, then the correct action is to delete the two fields from the V2 body rather than keep paying for them.
